question: Should OpenClaw ship a file-tool-only per-path policy that explicitly excludes arbitrary host `exec`, or should it require sandbox/OS containment before offering this security control?
rationale: The requested feature changes a security promise across filesystem tools, media loading, spawned agents, and shell execution; code review alone cannot choose the acceptable user-visible guarantee.

options.title: Ship an explicit file-tool policy
options.body: Define canonical `tools.fs.allowedPaths` and `tools.fs.denyPaths` with normalization and deny precedence, while documenting sandbox or OS isolation as required for arbitrary `exec`.

options.title: Require shell containment first
options.body: Defer the policy until the product can enforce an equivalent boundary around shell-mediated access and redirects.

options.title: Keep the current guardrails
options.body: Retain `workspaceOnly`, tool allow/deny, and sandbox guidance without adding a broader per-path host policy.

recommendation.title: Ship an explicit file-tool policy
recommendation.body: Define canonical `tools.fs.allowedPaths` and `tools.fs.denyPaths` with normalization and deny precedence, while documenting sandbox or OS isolation as required for arbitrary `exec`.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue’s existing maintainer-side review already owns the unresolved distinction between file-tool enforcement and arbitrary shell execution.
